title: Growing up in the Irish Channel; Army in 1917
summary: He grew up in the Irish Channel, where one club paraded until 1917, then went into the Army.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: What neighborhood did you say you were brought up in?
I was brought up in the Irish Channel. That's around Diamond and South Peter. Enunciation Street, Chappatula Street, St. Thomas Street.
Did they have many Carnival clubs up there when you were young?
No they didn't. We had one club up there. They were all in the back of town. Zulus, Canemys, Bulls, all those clubs were back here. Hop Goblins were all in the back of town.
What was the one up in Channel?

Well we had, we just had the, oh no, what the name was like that club. We paraded at that time, in that time, and then they, well that was around 17, 18, 19, 18, 1917, just before the war. Then during the war they broke up. Of course I left, when I went to the Army in 17, and when I come out the Army, I left for my neighborhood altogether. And I've been down here and down there ever since I've been down here for 50 years.
